newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian conservation group opposes power plants.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian conservation group opposes power plants.

text.p: The Norwegian Society for the Conservation of Nature is appealing against licences granted to Naturkraft AS for the construction of two gas-fired power stations in the southwest of Norway, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said on Thursday.
The Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Administration (NVE) gave Naturkraft the go-ahead on October 30 to build the country's first gas-fired power stations at Kaarstoe and Kollsnes.

Status Weekly said the group's appeal cited increased acid precipitation over western Norway, that gas-fired power stations with minimal utilisation of waste heat are very wasteful of resources and that the two plants will increase Norwegian emissions of carbon dioxide by 6.3 percent.
The two 350 megawatt plants will produce around 5.6 terrawatt hours per year and will cost around 3.6 billion crowns.
Naturkraft, set up specifically for the GAS PLANT project, is a joint-venture between Norsk Hydro ASA, Norway's largest electricity producer Statkraft A/S and Statoil.
